title: Multiple Mixture Model Response Optimizer
labelAnalysisTime: Be patient! Optimization may take longer with more models, more mixture components, or more random restarts.
modelselector1: Click one or more mixture models created by Analyze Mixture Design
labelModelResponseValues:
Mixture components used by the selected model, 
in the order Analyze Mixture Design recorded them
instructionLabel: Specify comma-separated values -- one value for each selected model, in the same order the models are listed above
goal: Goal: (Specify minimize, maximize, target, or range)
target: Target: Specify target values of the responses
lower: Lower: Specify minimum acceptable values of the responses (if left blank, the model's own fitted-value range is used)
upper: Upper: Specify maximum acceptable values of the responses (if left blank, the model's own fitted-value range is used)
weight: Weight: Specify weight values (penalty for being away from target); must be > 0, default 1
importance: Importance: Specify importance for combining multiple responses; must be > 0, default 1
totalAmount: Total amount (components must sum to this value, in the same units as the bounds below)
lowerBoundsInput: Lower bounds (optional -- comma-separated, one per component, in the SAME order shown above)
upperBoundsInput: Upper bounds (optional -- comma-separated, one per component, in the SAME order shown above)
lblBoundsNote: Optional. Leave BOTH fields blank to automatically use the minimum and maximum of each component observed in the first selected model's own fitting data. This works reliably for designs where the true bounds are actually reached by at least one run -- Simplex Lattice, Simplex Centroid, and Extreme Vertices designs all guarantee this by construction. WARNING: for a D-optimal-selected design, auto-derived bounds may be unreliable -- D-optimal point selection is not guaranteed to touch every true extreme, so the derived range could be narrower than actually intended. If your model was built from a D-optimal search, specify both bounds explicitly to guide the optimization correctly. Run once with any placeholder bounds to see the exact component order to use, if unsure.
numOfStartsNote: The search is a smooth local optimizer (optim, L-BFGS-B) applied to the mixture's free components, with the last component always computed from the sum-to-Total constraint. Multiple random restarts (default 20) reduce the chance of settling on a local rather than global optimum -- the same reasoning used elsewhere in this DOE suite for D-optimal search repeats.
randomseedsNote: Optional. Leave blank to use a different random starting configuration each time you run this (results may vary slightly run-to-run, since the restarts beyond the first are randomly generated). Specify a number for reproducible, identical results every time you re-run with the same inputs.
showEachModelPredictionChk: Show predicted response and individual desirability for each model at the optimum

help.title: Optimize Multiple Mixture Model Responses (Desirability)
help.body:
Description
Finds the mixture composition (component proportions summing to Total) that best satisfies one or more response goals simultaneously, combined via a Derringer-Suich composite desirability function -- the same desirability approach used by this suite's general-purpose response optimizers, but with a search mechanism built specifically for the sum-to-Total mixture constraint.

Why the general-purpose response optimizers don't work here
This suite's Multiple Model Response Optimizer and Multiple Response (same model formula) Optimizer both search using optim(method = "L-BFGS-B", lower =, upper =) -- independent box constraints on every predictor, with no way to express an equality constraint like A+B+C+D = Total. Given a mixture model, that search would happily evaluate points like A=40, B=40, C=40, D=40 (summing to 160), which are meaningless for a model only ever valid on the constrained simplex it was fit on. This dialog instead parameterizes the search over only q-1 free components, always computing the last component as Total minus the sum of the others, so every candidate point evaluated is guaranteed to sum to Total exactly.

Selecting models
Only select models created by Analyze Mixture Design (these carry component-name metadata this dialog checks automatically). All selected models must share the identical set of mixture components -- if you select models built from different components, the dialog stops with a clear error rather than searching a meaningless combined space.

Mixture Setup
Total amount and component bounds must be supplied directly here (in the same units used to fit the models) -- unlike Augment Mixture Design, there is no existing design dataset here to automatically derive bounds from.

Composite Desirability
D = (d1^w1 x d2^w2 x ... )^(1/sum(w)), the geometric mean of each response's individual desirability (0 to 1), weighted by Importance. D = 0 if any single response completely fails its goal; D = 1 only if every response fully meets its goal simultaneously.
